title: Cohort Harm-Reduction Schematic and Ops Playbook (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for running harm-reduction focused micro-rollouts and A/B slices for latency-sensitive LLM features. The centerline here is: reduce blast radius by treating cohorts as first-class citizens, apply automated mitigations for behavioral drift, and make operator tooling explicit and simple to follow during the first 48 hours of exposure.

Audience:
- Product owners launching LLM-driven UX changes
- Console operators and oncall engineers
- Solutions engineers running proofs-of-concept with customers

High-level approach (short):
1) Define cohorts by risk vector (permissions, content type, geography, usage intensity).
2) Synthetic-shadow baseline traffic from each cohort into canary variants (no user-facing change) to surface early regressions.
3) Gate progressive exposure with automated metrics + manual guardrails.
4) If a safety signal fires, run the harm-reduction script (quarantine cohort, route to fallback, preserve telemetry).

Cohort schematic (notes):
- Risk tiers: low / medium / high (heuristics: high = judged-sensitive content, admin users, high spend).
- Cohort attributes to capture: user_id_hash, plan_tier, request_type, model_family, route, region, feature_flags_active.
- Example cohort groups: onboarding-beta, search-rerank-synthetic, billing-invoices, enterprise-demo-seat.
- Each cohort must have owner and a rollback contact (oncall alias + product owner).

Synthetic shadowing plan: why and how
- Why: surface behavioral drift (hallucination rate, safety classifier score drop, embeddings shift) without exposing users.
- How: mirror 0.5%–5% of live requests depending on cost profile into candidate model(s). Run determinism checks and difference metrics every 15m.
- Execution notes: throttled playback, preserve original user context, anonymize PII, use sampling stratified by cohort.

Telemetry and primary signals (kept intentionally small):
- Quality signals (rolling 1h / 24h): manual review failure rate (% flagged by human), automated safety classifier fail rate, policy filter hits.
- Latency/cost signals: p50/p95 latency change vs baseline, CPU/GPU utilization, token cost per request.
- Stability signals: server error rate (5xx), retry multiplier, KV-cache miss rate (relevant for cached prefix benefits).
- Business signals: conversion delta, retention indicators for affected cohort (24h lookback).
- Drift signals: embedding cosine similarity median vs baseline, output token entropy shift.

Example thresholds for automated gates (tunable):
- p95 latency increase > 30% sustained for 10m -> gate
- 5xx rate increase > 0.5 percentage points over baseline -> gate
- Safety classifier fail rate increase > 50% relative -> gate
- Manual-review failure rate > 1% in first 1k outputs -> gate
- Embedding median cosine drop > 0.12 -> gate

Quarantine & harm-reduction play (step-by-step):
1) Alert fires -> steward (oncall) acknowledges within 5m. Add incident tag: ROLLOUT-COHORT-<id>.
2) Reduce exposure: flip cohort's weight to 0% or route to fallback model via feature flag. Document action in Slack channel #rollouts.
3) Preserve data: snapshot 1h of inputs/outputs (redact PII) and export to secure s3 for debug.
4) Run triage checklist (below). If behavioral issue -> escalate to product and ML applied-research.
5) If cause is config/caching -> hotfix and re-enable 10% then ramp. If cause is model behavior -> rollback to pinned model and begin postmortem.

Triage checklist (fast):
- Confirm cohort identity and traffic slice size.
- Check model revision and quantization profile.
- Is there concurrent infra change? (kernel, runtime, routing).
- Check synthetic shadow diffs for recent drift.
- Run quick A/B of fallback vs candidate on a replay pool.
- Note: capture failure repro steps into Jira ticket and link to ROLLOUT-<id>.

Operational scripts & alert templates (examples):
- Slack alert body (short):
  [ALERT] Canary gate fired: cohort=onboarding-beta, metric=p95-latency, delta=+42%, action=quarantine
  Owner: @maya.patel @oncall-console
  Quick links: [canary dashboard] [replay dataset] [rollback button]

- Shell snippet (ops):
  # reduce cohort weight to zero (example)
  curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://console.redwood.ai/api/rollouts/act -d '{"cohort":"onboarding-beta","action":"set_weight","weight":0}'

Design notes for staggered exposure:
- Micro-ramp cadence: 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with 30–90m observation windows. For high-risk cohorts, increase windows.
- Interleave synthetic-only waves (shadow) before any user-facing exposure.
- Prefer horizontal cohort expansion to avoid sudden capacity shifts (i.e., more cohorts at small weights vs whole population at medium weight).

Analytics & experiments hygiene:
- Always register the rollout as an experiment with hypothesis, primary metric, and a safety metric. Tag dataset snapshots with experiment id.
- Use deterministic bucketing for cohort assignment to ensure stable A/B populations.
- Mandatory post-launch review: 72h slate with checklist: signal review, customer tickets, cost impact.

Human-in-loop checkpoints (where to force a pause):
- If the cohort contains a legal or compliance tranche (billing/legal contacts).
- If conversion or revenue signals are primary metrics.
- Any time a manual review queue grows beyond a threshold (e.g., >100 items outstanding).

Runbook caveats & operational tradeoffs (notes):
- Cost vs sensitivity: heavier synthetic shadowing catches more issues early but increases token spend; tradeoff should be documented per experiment.
- Overfitting to synthetic tests is possible; keep at least one human-review sample from live traffic for first 24h.
- Avoid changing more than one major axis (model family, quantization, routing) in the same rollout wave.

Open questions / TODOs (work items):
- Finalize standard cohort attribute set and upstream schema (data infra work: see PLAT-5797).
- Instrument an embedding drift test harness that runs in the console automatically.
- Add a small UX affordance for enterprise customers to opt into canary program with explicit consent.
- Create a curated quick-playbook template in the Console for common rollback reasons.

Links & references (quick):
- Confluence: PLAT-5797 - "Cohort schema and enrichment"
- Jira: ROLL-312 - "Onboarding-beta canary plan"
- GH: repo/PR#482 - "canary routing + weight API"

Notes to self / shorthand:
- Keep the initial signal set intentionally small; expand only after stable baselining.
- Prefer small, reproducible synthetic tests over broad fuzzing in first 72h.
- Make the quarantine action reversible and observable in the Console (audit log!).

---
End of draft. This is intentionally rough; looking for feedback on: what are the minimum telemetry fields for cohort alignment, a sensible default micro-ramp cadence for medium risk, and whether synthetic shadowing should be on by default for Dedicated customers. Please add comments inline or ping in #rollouts.
